items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: the following weekend, Herbie Nichols -- I was able to play with him

ctx.x: Things kind of slowed up, and I worked a couple of gigs down at the Fire Spot Fireside and Dave Amram Amarand had a weekend down there with me, and I was in the rhythm section, and it was just a little hamburger joint on the Bowery there; we were

trying to make a little club out of it, and the next weekend, Ray Bryant came in on piano, and the following weekend, Herbie Nichols -- I was able to play with him; he was a genius. Beautiful young man -- not too long before he died. And then Thelonious said, "Come on down," and we with Trane and Shadow went down there, and we played -- and that was the gig. I stayed with that gig, plus recordings, first record it, still at Riverside now, and one night we had a recording date with Gerry Mulligan and Monk, called…

So I went around to this little place and got me a -- I'll never forget -- I should have gotten a hot sandwich, but I got a tunafish salad, ate it, and oh boy, it ate the pit of my stomach and I was sick; so sick I was afraid and I just took a taxi. I made a call ... I called up one of the bass players that lived right around the corner from me, and asked him if he would work in my place, and I went on home. Keepnews
